source_title: 10 Skydance Offers Voluntary Buyouts, Moves To Five-Day In-Office Policy Across Company
source_excerpt:

Starz Q3 Revenue Grows, Losses Narrow As It Starts To Unlock “Financial Upside Of Increased Ownership” In Slate
The new Skydance co-CEOs David Ellison and Ynon Kreitz on Monday revealed plans to move the full complement of staffers to five days a week in office in person and offered a Voluntary Buyout (VBO) Program “to give eligible employees the option to move on in a way that works for them.”
“We truly believe this is in the best interest of our company and our people. We’ve seen the benefits firsthand at Paramount, and we want every part of Skydance to share in them,” they said in a memo obtained by Deadline (read it in full below).
David Ellison, Ynon Kreiz Praise Staff, Lay Out Priorities For New Skydance: “Getting Here Has Been Quite A Journey”
Skydance Co-CEO Ynon Kreiz Says Jobs Cuts Will Be Handled “Respectfully, Transparently” As Company Restructures
Paramount-Skydance had already resumed a five day in-office work week. WBD was still at three days.
The return to office transition would be phased in over time depending on location. The merged company’s largest real estate areas are in Los Angeles, New York, Atlanta and London. Watch on Deadline
The announcement reflects one of many major shifts since Skydance closed its $110-billion acquisition of WBD earlier this month. The combined entity carries a hefty debt load of near $90 billion in a climate of rising interest rates and Ellison has committed to at least $2 billion in cost savings, a chunk of which will come from layoffs. As the cost of servicing the debt rises, the cuts may need to go deeper. Voluntary buyouts are often the first step in a process of winnowing down staff.
“As we bring our teams together, we recognize that not everyone will see their future here, and we respect that. To give eligible employees the option to move on in a way that works for them, we are introducing a Voluntary Buyout (VBO) Program. Those who qualify will receive an individual communication with their personalized details and terms, and a window to decide whether to accept this one-time offer,” the memo reads.
Team, At Skydance, our goal is to build the next-generation media and entertainment company, powered by creativity and technology. We are creative-first, audience focused, tech-forward and globally scaled. And in a world of endless choice and fierce competition for attention, we don’t just want to succeed. We want to win. To do that, we must be a strong, connected and agile company. Among our business and creative priorities, none matters more than building a strong culture, because it’s the foundation of everything we want to achieve. Winning requires us to work as one team: one company, fully aligned. That means communicating openly and collaborating efficiently across every part of the organization. In-Person Collaboration We believe in-person collaboration is vital to our culture and to the success of our business. Especially in a creative company like ours, the best ideas come from people in the same room, sharing perspectives, challenging one another and solving problems. Being together isn’t just about showing up. It’s about inspiring one another, learning and coaching, forming friendships and having the casual conversations that spark something great. With that in mind, we will adopt a five-day in-office policy across all of Skydance. We truly believe this is in the best interest of our company and our people. We’ve seen the benefits firsthand at Paramount, and we want every part of Skydance to share in them. While many of you are already in the office five days a week, we understand this may be a significant change to the daily routines of others. To give you time to plan and adjust, we will take a phased approach by location. You will receive ample notice before changes take effect, and we will work closely with managers to support you through the transition. Voluntary Buyout Program As we bring our teams together, we recognize that not everyone will see their future here, and we respect that. To give eligible employees the option to move on in a way that works for them, we are introducing a Voluntary Buyout (VBO) Program. Those who qualify will receive an individual communication with their personalized details and terms, and a window to decide whether to accept this one-time offer. We recognize this is a significant decision, and we want you to feel informed and supported. If this applies to you, please review your materials carefully and reach out to your leadership or HR representative with any questions. FAQs and other resources are available on the Skydance Integration or Ask Employee Connection on WBD One. Please know we don’t take any of this lightly. We are clear about what we’re building: a company that tells the stories people around the world love, embraces new ways to connect with audiences, and leads the next era of media and entertainment. We have the talent, the creative firepower and the ambition to do it, and we will get there together. Thank you for your commitment, and for the creativity and passion you bring to your work every day. Best, David and Ynon
